title: Study evaluating the efficacy and safety of daridorexant in patients with major depressive disorder and insomnia.
official: Efficacy and Safety of Daridorexant in Patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Insomnia: Double-blind, randomized, controlled trial
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of Daridorexant in improving insomnia assessed with the ISI in MDD patients at 3 months.
conditions: Patients with major depressive episode and moderate to severe insomnia disorder
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age Range: 18-99 years old.
2. Patients with a current major depressive episode according to DSM-5, in a stable phase (defined as at least 4 weeks without significant changes in antidepressant treatment and no psychiatric hospitalizations in the previous 8 weeks) and with moderate or greater severity, as indicated by a total score of ≥ 20 on the Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS).
3. Insomnia disorder confirmed according to DSM-5
4. Informed Consent: Ability and willingness to provide written informed consent.
5. Acceptance of Protocol Requirements: Agreement to adhere to all scheduled visits, treatment plans, and study procedures.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Other Current Psychiatric Disorders: Any current psychiatric disorder other than major depressive disorder (e.g., active psychotic disorders, mania, hypomania, acute schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder).
2. Concomitant Use with Moderate and potent CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Prohibited due to potential drug interaction (refer to protocol section 4.5 for specifics).
3. Moderate and severe hepatic Impairment: Any hepatic condition deemed unsafe for daridorexant use.
4. Relapse or Worsening of the Main Diagnosis: Relapse of depression whose severity precludes continued participation according to the investigator’s judgment.
5. Substance Use Disorder: History of substance use disorder without sustained remission. Exception: past sedative abuse may be permissible if remission criteria are clearly met, as determined by the investigator.
6. Excessive Caffeine Intake: Daily consumption of >400 mg of caffeine (e.g., >4 standard cups of coffee).
7. High-Risk Alcohol Consumption: Alcohol intake above recommended risk thresholds (i.e., >4 standard drinks/day for men, >2 standard drinks/day for women).
8. Use of Non-Permitted Sleep Medications: Concurrent use of melatonin, benzodiazepines, sedative antidepressants or sedative antipsychotics use for insomnia not allowed by the protocol and unwillingness to follow the slow-taper schedule constitutes an exclusion criterion.
9. No concurrent sleep medications at least 30 days prior to baseline. Exclusion criteria if the patient has withdrawal symptoms and/or sleep disturbances measured by BWSQ prior to baseline.
10. Uncontrolled Severe Medical Conditions: Any condition that could interfere with study procedures, safety, or outcome measures (e.g., unstable cardiovascular, respiratory, neurological, or endocrine disorders).
11. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
12. Cognitive Impairments: Significant impairments that prevent the comprehension or completion of study questionnaires or procedures.
13. Hypersensitivity: Known allergy or hypersensitivity to daridorexant or any of its excipients.
14. Specific Sleep Disorders: Sleep apnea or hypopnea index ≥ 15 events/hour (based on American Academy of Sleep Medicine criteria) or any event associated with oxygen saturation < 80% (as measured by polysomnography).
15. Periodic limb movement index ≥ 15 events/hour (as measured by polysomnography). Restless legs syndrome, circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders, REM behavior disorder, or narcolepsy.
